newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine rebel leader casts a vote for peace.
newsitem.headline: Philippine rebel leader casts a vote for peace.

text.p: Philippine rebel leader Nur Misuari formally entered mainstream political life on Monday by voting in elections where he is the sole candidate for the governorship of a Moslem autonomous regional government.

"This vote symbolises our commitment to peace, democracy and progress for our people here in Mindanao and eventually for the entire country," said Misuari, who signed a peace deal with the government last week ending a 24-year separatist war in the southern Philippines.
In a live nationwide broadcast, Philippine television showed Misuari casting his ballot in a school in his home town of Jolo on the southern island of Sulu.
The former university professor turned revolutionary is running for the governorship of the Autonomous Region of Moslem Mindanao, which covers just four southern provinces.
Under his peace deal with Manila, he will also head a Southern Philippine Council for Peace and Development covering the whole of the main southern island of Mindanao and nearby islands.
The council, bitterly opposed by some southern Philippine Christians, is envisaged as the precursor of a much wider autonomous regional government.
